sections.heading: Managed shadow retired
sections.text: Automatic managed TCG shadow admission was disabled on 20 November at 07:36 UTC. Required Agentplane VM CI runs on the self-hosted BuildBuddy kvm-vm pool. The managed and KVM results below are the archived comparison.

sections.heading: All 100 manual pairs
sections.text: Both routes passed on the first attempt in 76 pairs. Only managed TCG failed first in 22 pairs, only KVM in one, and both in one. Eighteen of 23 managed first-attempt failures and both KVM first-attempt failures recovered on retry. Final failures were 5 of 100 on managed and 0 of 100 on KVM. The 100 pairs include 89 distinct commits.

sections.heading: Failure signatures
sections.text: Managed first attempts hit 14 Sandbox readiness deadlines, seven guest shutdown failures, and two interrupted session setups. Some also refused recycling with a remaining Sandbox. The two KVM first-attempt failures recorded a VMI lookup failure with a later refused Kubernetes API connection (pair 64), and guest shutdown failure (pair 71). Both scenarios passed on retry.

sections.heading: Devel push pairs
sections.text: Both routes passed both scenarios on their first Bazel attempt in the three fresh pre-cutover pairs and the one fresh post-cutover pair. The post-cutover workflow recorded successful CI and comparison jobs. Its failed job published the Agentplane App image.

vm_shadow_review.selection_note: The pre-cutover census yielded three fresh pairs among 68 pushes. After cutover and through the disable time, 31 pushes yielded 19 cached required KVM results, 11 archives without a required invocation and one fresh completed pair. At review, each run had a collector archive.
vm_shadow_review.sample_note: Completed manual batch on 20 November 2026, 03:11–07:05 UTC. All 100 pairs ran the Claude and Codex VM scenarios on 89 distinct commits. The comparison used the original two routing targets, with up to six pairs in flight. Earlier manual snapshots retain their original windows.

scope: Read-only diagnosis and report publication. No workflow reruns, CI policy/source changes, deployments, or scheduled monitoring.

findings.title: VM cold setup consumes the case deadline
findings.classification: Accounting repair merged and controlled; guest boot failure remains separate
findings.frequency: 3 / 10 failed VM target verdicts have cold setup and the 600-second deadline; overlapping seven-day population.
findings.observation: 54d9f029: setup 375.019s (baseline missing_marker), 25 serial image imports with a 324.902s elapsed envelope, then concurrent Claude/Codex cases. Claude ran 229.839s; all its turn waits completed before pytest interrupted it. The outer deadline included setup. Two earlier failures, e995fe1b and 44881c80, show the same cumulative-budget pattern. These are distinct from the 300-second silent guest waits.
findings.comparator: Fresh neighbouring pass 26a37e83 reused the same baseline fingerprint, setup 51.405s, Claude 138.281s and Codex 124.111s; its JUnit has two passing cases. Source and TestRunner action digest differ, so this is a phase comparator, not same-source recovery or a controlled speedup. Earlier fresh cold pass 35e28298 had 102.177s setup; its XML is unavailable.
findings.repair: PR #17261 separates case_timeout from pytest item timeout and reports native JUnit call durations. Five accounting regressions pass; the scaled old-policy control fails during shared setup. Rebased required CI is green, with a fresh cold VM pass. The newly traced pre-Runtime boot/cleanup failure is the next engineering lead; see the 17 November follow-up. Native profile capture is merged (#17327); a separate fully cold 25-image control now supplies complete bounded artifacts. See the selected experiments without changing this historical denominator.
findings.limit: Historical 3/10 count and source/window are unchanged. Selected post-change executions have different sources/state and do not establish a fleet latency or failure-rate improvement.

findings.title: Managed VM infrastructure retries still hide failures
findings.classification: Observed infrastructure failures; lower cause unresolved
findings.frequency: 12 UNAVAILABLE execution rows among 161 unique linked VM execution IDs in the 149 non-cached-result cohort; selected physical population, not a fleet flake rate.
findings.observation: Seven pause-socket refusals, three VM-health deadlines, one TSC restore signature, and one other snapshot/vCPU restore failure preceded final verdicts. Eleven affected target outcomes ultimately passed; one failed its separate OOM assertion. A thirteenth infrastructure row is cancellation and has a target PASSED summary without a matching successful execution row. Keep that mapping boundary visible. Two additional target-history failures-to-build are outside these 149 results: TSC scaling EINVAL and VM health failure.
findings.comparator: The current source still uses managed RBE for the required VM target. Manual KVM/Firecracker and worker-image experiments in sibling reports have different placement, coverage and resource conditions; their passes do not repair these failures.
findings.repair: Use provider execution diagnostics to retain snapshot creator, source/restore CPU and TSC metadata and the last guest kernel state before pause refusal. Separate restore, active guest failure and post-execution pause failures. Validate any provider/kernel repair on matched fresh actions and at representative contention, preserving the real VM lifecycle.
findings.limit: A pause socket refusal alone does not prove a kernel panic. Failed result traces do not supply the provider kernel or snapshot producer; no new provider root cause or routing recommendation is established.

findings.title: Keep browser failure mechanisms separate
findings.classification: Destination readiness repair merged; separate browser startup trigger remains unresolved
findings.frequency: 3 failed thread-browser verdicts in the stats API slice of 74 runs, plus 1 / 76 thread-window verdicts. The API denominator is cache-filtered target tracking, not a physical exposure census.
findings.observation: c210960a reproduces History/direct/fresh Electric cursor 334 while DOM remains 264 before route-lifetime repair #16051. Its final live GET raced route removal. Separate 80e31b7f fails thread navigation: metadata names the destination, but message 129 is absent at the default 5s assertion. Existing browser marks show new rows and tail layout arrive much later than destination metadata. 5699ac4c fails before the lost-HTTP-reply scenario starts: open_browser shares a 30s timeout across opened.get() and page.goto(); the timeout fires in page.goto. Later close/unsubscribe cancellation is downstream. ed5acdf3 ends at Bazel TIMEOUT with only a partial test log.
findings.comparator: The earlier final route-lifetime candidate passed ten distinct remote streaming attempts, retaining cursor, anchor and draft assertions. The new seven-day window overlaps that intervention; no matched post-fix browser physical denominator was collected. A later navigation failure is a different case and cannot refute or validate that specific repair.
findings.repair: PR #17307 now waits for the destination message with the existing standard predicate helper; streaming, tail, cursor, anchor, draft and lost-reply assertions remain. PR #17305 adds open/proxy phases. The historical setup await was held in Playwright post-action snapshot instrumentation after successful navigation; bounded controls narrow, but do not identify, its natural trigger. See selected experiments.
findings.limit: The navigation record supports a readiness boundary, not a proven frontend race or justification for longer global waits. Natural login ReadTimeout from earlier selected PR runs remains unresolved.

findings.title: Two build regressions were sustained, not flaky
findings.frequency: 5 consecutive invocations with the removed lock helper; 2 consecutive invocations with a stale package label. These account for all 7 BUILD_FAILURE invocations.
findings.observation: 14 Nov 20:09–20:49 UTC: environment_grants_integration_test.go referenced waitForAdvisoryWaiter after its deletion. #16405 introduced the scenario-owned wait helper. 13 Nov 11:48–11:56 UTC: central_sampler/cmd/BUILD.bazel still referenced removed environment_runtime_transport; #16218 corrected startup-test wiring after the peer-TLS package move.
findings.comparator: Both repairs are in the inspected source, which now places dispatcher tests under session_dispatcher. These source confirmations establish current wiring, not an attributed fleet reliability gain.
findings.repair: Keep the historical failures classified as regressions. When moving or deleting shared test helpers, audit all test targets and BUILD references and compile every affected test package. No duplicate repair is recommended.
findings.limit: Other test failures can co-occur with a build regression; 44881c80 also has a VM timeout.

findings.title: A red-at-merge run lost its outer observer
findings.classification: New transport incident; final remote result unknown
findings.frequency: 1 of 3 devel PRs with a red gate visibly completed before merge; 3 / 1,487 devel merges. This is operator friction, not a flake rate.
findings.observation: #16365 tested synthetic merge efaf8d8234e26e19054dfeebc301341d8ad3b254, distinct from head 0ab74f20488434ef3b47f1743c0987a94cea14c2. At 17:34:07 UTC the outer observer reported INTERNAL, stream closed with task still claimed. Child 0582b45b is DISCONNECTED; the log had 239/246 test verdicts. Execution lookup returned no rows.
findings.comparator: Prior accepted-run reconciliation controls demonstrated same-ID observation after injected observer loss, but the CLI patch was unshipped in that historical report. Native inner Execute/WaitExecution loss is a separate issue.
findings.repair: BuildBuddy CLI repair is parked by the operator. Retain this historical incident and its unknown result; it is not an active implementation recommendation.
findings.limit: This incident does not establish a passing original remote command or a duplicate submission. No explicit merge override was identified in queried timelines/comments; organization audit evidence was unavailable.

findings.title: Debundle failures include an already-retired budget gate
findings.classification: Historical assertion contract and source drift; no verified randomness
findings.frequency: 2 Excalidraw report-count failures plus 1 memory-budget failure in three mainline invocations.
findings.observation: 15 Nov: vendor_swap_report_lists_every_mark expected 9 references but observed 10 in two consecutive commits. Current source asserts complete vendor sections and a positive rewrite count, while retaining emitted-JavaScript behavior probes. 16 Nov 23:25 UTC: source_fact_memory_test passed output preservation, then exceeded its 200 MiB child RSS budget; integer formatting printed both observed and budget as 200 MiB.
findings.comparator: #17117 merged after the observation window and moved the memory benchmark to a manual benchmark owner. The inspected source contains that move. This changes required coverage; it does not lower memory use or prove the benchmark intrinsically flaky.
findings.repair: Do not repeat the retired required-gate recommendation. Measure the manual memory benchmark with real profiling, raw KiB and fixed inputs if the resource budget is still a product requirement. Keep the emitted-JavaScript behavior tests required.
findings.limit: No same-source fresh retry was inspected for either Debundle failure; no flaky classification or measured repair is claimed.

prior_lanes.topic: Recover completed RBE results after execution-stream loss
prior_lanes.prior_observation: Native Bazel recovered one injected gRPC INTERNAL after its first Operation using one Execute and one same-ID WaitExecution. Two interruptions exhausted remote_retries=1: one physical test passed, but Bazel exited 34 with no TestResult. This is a sufficient false-red mechanism, not proof of the natural RST_STREAM cause.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Next natural false-red: private narrowly enabled native remote_grpc_log; summarize first Operation, Execute/WaitExecution statuses and retry consumption, correlate exact provider operation. Separate Wait-only retry budget is an upstream candidate requiring cancellation/Execute replay controls.

prior_lanes.topic: Validate KVM placement for required Agentplane VM CI
prior_lanes.prior_observation: Seven physical actions / 31 JUnit cases passed. Four KVM actions shared three registered slots; the fourth queued 215.314s and finished 66.668s after the managed VM. Pod finished last, giving zero VM-only fixed-clock headroom. The newer-source repeat is not a matched graph.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Run at least three bounded bursts, each equivalent to four concurrent PRs, on literal source pins. Include one after natural scale-down to one registered worker; observe all required GitHub gates and isolation.

prior_lanes.topic: Eliminate avoidable cold Agentplane system-test baseline rebuilds
prior_lanes.prior_observation: The 12-head census found 36 target opportunities: 18 absent, three unavailable, three cached and 12 fresh suite outcomes, with 15 unique physical IDs. Six of 12 fresh baselines were cold; all cleaned up. Old artifacts did not record why. The merged span records reuse/rebuild reasons without retaining extra mutable state.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh retained-suite outcomes, whichever is later. Keep cached, failed and missing outcomes separate; group by backend, worker, compatibility key, fingerprint and rebuild reason.

prior_lanes.topic: Skip unchanged OCI imports only when the image is usable
prior_lanes.prior_observation: Nine real native usability guard cases passed. Same-worker warm ABBA setup averaged 46.992s control versus 32.216s candidate, 14.776s shorter. Both selected graphs passed the identical 27 cases. Their 458.570s / 472.642s Bazel times are not causal evidence: VM root-image inputs differed and order/cache exposure were unmatched.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Keep issue #16028 open. Within seven days after merge or on the next naturally selected backend head, compare matched warm/cold complete graphs and exact-head required gates. Record source/CAS and cache identities, native phases, CPU, peak memory and capacity. Resolve the VM generated-root input mismatch before comparing VM results.

prior_lanes.topic: Shorten MCP Actions execution with isolated case resources
prior_lanes.prior_observation: All five real MCP cases passed in each source-matched ABBA arm. Mean case envelope fell from 112.336s to 96.833s, but whole action grew from 254.348s to 265.866s and CPU also rose. Baselines were warm/warm/warm/cold across different workers. Five peak Sandboxes exactly fit the existing cap; no action, compute or CI win is established.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: After adoption, collect seven complete UTC days or the first 50 fresh MCP executions, whichever is later. Compare case execution, setup, CPU, scheduling and the last required gate, with cache, retry, baseline-state and tested-source groups kept separate.

prior_lanes.topic: Test read-only harness artifact mounts to avoid OCI unpacking
prior_lanes.prior_observation: Claude and Codex each completed instructed and plain turns in fresh Sandboxes with 44 read-only native artifact mounts and fresh writable homes; cleanup passed. Declared inputs total 914,451,230 bytes versus 914,498,274 packaged, only 47,044 bytes less. One unmatched pair observed less unpack/setup work, but no meaningful input-byte saving or causal CI gain.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Keep issue #16030 open. On the next relevant backend head or within seven days of the feasibility pass, compare counterbalanced complete Pod/MCP/VM graphs while retaining real packaged-image boot coverage. Match source/CAS and cache exposure; measure required gates, per-Sandbox mounts, lazy artifact reads and resource cost.

prior_lanes.topic: Diagnose and repair silent progress loss in VM CI guests
prior_lanes.prior_observation: A fresh natural failure aborted QEMU at guest uptime 1.773s with an iotlb_to_section assertion; replacement scenario passed but original shutdown receipt was missing. Separate issue #16057 tracks the crash. Two fresh VM passes used three physical actions because one provider pause failed. The original 300s admitted-turn stall did not recur; late live triggers remain unexercised.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: On the next admitted-turn stall, correlate live samples at 210 and 240 seconds for the same Sandbox UID with Runtime history and independent serial output before cleanup. Review seven days of non-cached physical exposure; the original stall remains open.

prior_lanes.topic: Diagnose and repair browser login fixture stalls
prior_lanes.prior_observation: Three fresh browser cases passed with six successful auth exchanges (40–131ms). Holding actual TLS OIDC discovery for 5.25s caused AppProcess.authenticate to time out after 5.002s before page interaction, with client, Go and provider phases retained. This faithful hop control does not reproduce the unknown natural cause or show a lower failure rate.
prior_lanes.next_measurement: Next natural failure: join client trace ID to Go phases and provider path/port to locate first missing hop; seven-day count of non-cached physical setup outcomes, separate cached rows.

prior_lanes.topic: Locate and repair browser history projection lag
prior_lanes.prior_observation: New natural failure had committed/direct/fresh Electric cursor 334 versus DOM 264; its final live GET began 2.298ms after last-route removal.
